title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect: Eph 1 seems to make acceptance eternal before faith
pass_a_gloss: There can also be brought forward from the Scriptures some places which seem, as regards the elect, to assert an actual reconciliation with God, and that an eternal one, before their faith and repentance. Ephesians 1:4: God is said to have elected them before the foundation of the world, and in verse 6 to have had them accepted in his beloved Son: Therefore they were elect, and already actually justified and reconciled from eternity: nor was their reconciliation on God’s part made after faith applied to the Gospel, but rather then it began to be manifested and revealed, which had been done before the foundations of the world were laid.
pass_b_english: Some Scripture places can also be brought forward that seem, as to the elect, to assert an actual reconciliation with God—and an eternal one—before their faith and repentance.

Ephesians 1:4 says God elected them before the world’s foundation, and verse 6 that he had them accepted in his beloved Son. So, the objection runs, they were elect, and already actually justified and reconciled from eternity. Their reconciliation on God’s side was not made after faith was applied to the gospel; rather, what had already been done before the world’s foundations were laid then began to be manifested and revealed.
source_text:
Proferri etiam possunt ex Scripturis loca nonnulla quae videntur quoad electos actualem cum Deo reconciliationem, eamque aeternam, asserere; ante fidem & paenitentiam eorundem.

Ephes. i. 4. Deus dicitur eos elegisse ante mundi constitutionem, & versu 6. acceptos habuisse in dilecto suo Filio: Fuerunt igitur electi, & jam actu justificati & reconciliati ab aeterno: neque reconciliatio illorum ex parte Dei post fidem Evangelio adhibitam facta est, sed potius tum incepit manifestari & revelari, quod factum fuit ante jacta mundi fundamenta.
